"Zither Goddess, if I intended to deceive you, I wouldn't have gone to such lengths to reveal my identity after all the effort I put into convincing you that I am a Dragon Emperor, let alone bring up Tian Kai.
What could I possibly gain from doing this?" "That's..." Tan Songyun couldn't refute his logic.
"As a matter of fact, I am currently targeted by the Celestial Emperor, so it's incredibly risky for me to reveal myself.
However, I couldn't bear seeing you suffer because of some false rumors.
Zither Goddess, I will ask you again."
"Is your faith in Tian Kai—in me—that little?"
Tan Songyun trembled before falling silent, her expression reflecting the turmoil of an existential crisis.

chapters.title: Chapter 1761 Tan Songyun’s Decision
paragraphs: Tan Songyun recalled every moment of the year she had spent with Tian Kai—the emotions that had consumed her, the warmth of his presence, and the touch of his fingers on her body.

Then, she remembered the countless rumors she had heard about Tian Kai over tens of thousands of years, along with the hatred and anger that had festered within her. While the year she had spent with Tian Kai had been filled with joy, she couldn't simply cast aside the anguish and betrayal that had consumed her for thousands of years, as if it had never existed.
Even if the rumors were untrue and Tian Kai was innocent, the anguish Tan Songyun had endured was undeniably real and couldn't simply be dismissed.
'Tian Kai was innocent...? Then what have I been doing all these years? What am I doing with my life now?'
After a very long moment of silence, Tan Songyun suddenly smacked herself in the face and shook it off.

"Even after tens of thousands of years of feeling betrayed, it is undeniable that I still love Tian Kai to a certain extent, and if it turns out that all of the rumors I've heard about him are false, I will atone for my crimes."
"However, there's no way for me to confirm your words as of this moment, and I am no longer foolish enough to believe everything I hear. Therefore, I am going to follow and watch you to confirm it."
"You're going to follow me?" Yuan's eyes widened at her words.
"What's with that look? You don't want me to? Are you afraid I might expose the real you?" Tan Songyun frowned.
"No... that's not it. Didn't you hear me? I am currently being hunted by the Celestial Emperor. I also have many enemies. If you stay with me, I cannot guarantee your safety."
"So what? Even if I die in the process, I will not have any regrets—except that I won't be able to find out the truth."
Yuan rubbed his eyes and sighed, "I will also be traversing dangerous places."
"This won't be my first time visiting someplace dangerous."
Seeing how stubborn Tan Songyun was acting, Yuan said, "Fine, you can follow me, but the moment I deem you as a burden, I'll immediately leave you behind."
"Like you did back then?" Tan Songyun sneered.
"Even if you follow me, how will you determine what I said is true or false?" Yuan then asked.
"That's not something you need to know," she said.
Yuan removed the formation shortly after and called Xi Meili back.
"Well, since you're going to be following us, we might as well do an introduction," said Yuan.
"You may know me as Tian Kai, but my name now is Yuan. Are you aware of the existence of players?"
"Players... you mean the Outsiders?"
Yuan nodded and said, "I am one of them, as I was reborn in that world."

"You claim to have reincarnated, but why would you still retain Tian Kai's memories? As far as I know, those who reincarnate lose all memories of their past lives," Tan Songyun asked, her tone filled with doubt.
"My case is a little special. Also, not everyone forgets their memories. There are special techniques out there that help people regain their lost memories," Yuan explained.
Xi Meili introduced herself next, "My name is Xi Meili, and I am a real dragon. My bloodline is also royalty."
Tan Songyun's eyes widened, and she asked, "How are you related to the Xi Family in the upper heavens?"
"I don't know since I came from the Ancient Dragon City."
"Ancient Dragon City...? Never heard of that place."
"Anyway, I am Tan Songyun, and my relationship with Tian Kai here is—"
Tan Songyun gave Xi Meili a brief explanation of the situation, leaving her bewildered by the sheer strangeness of the events that unfolded.

"Um... me saying this probably won't mean anything at this point, but there is simply no way these rumors about Yuan are true. If you spend even a little time with him, you'd understand what I mean," said Xi Meili.
Tan Songyun narrowed her eyes at Xi Meili for a moment before asking, "What is your relationship with Tian Kai, anyway?"
"Once again, Tian Kai is dead. I am now Yuan."
"We're traveling companions," said Xi Meili.
"Just traveling companions?"
"For now, yes..."
"For now?" Tan Songyun raised an eyebrow.
"A-anyway, now that we've acquired the second Ancient Seal, what are we going to do next?" Xi Meili turned to look at Yuan, clearly trying to change the subject.
Yuan pondered for a moment before summoning Yin and Yang.
"Can you two figure out where the other two seals are?" Yuan asked them.
"We'll try," they responded simultaneously before disappearing into thin air.
Tan Songyun then asked, "Why didn't you ask the Dragon King where the other holders are?"
"Because even the holders themselves are unaware of the identities of the other holders," Yuan explained.
"By the way, how far have you managed to ascend, Zither Goddess?" Yuan then asked her.
"Can you stop calling me by that nickname? I don't like it."
"If you stop calling me Tian Kai. Ah, I almost forgot. Yuan is my real name. I currently go by Xiao Yang. Also, how should I address you if not Zither Goddess?"
"Anything but Zither Goddess. I no longer qualify for such a title."
"Then how about I continue addressing you as Lady Tan?"
"Do as you please. And I've reached all the way to the Supreme Heaven."
"The Ninth Heaven? That's impressive. Well, since we're trying to reach the Seventh Heaven as soon as possible, we might as well ascend to the Sixth Heaven now," said Yuan.
"Already? This will be your quickest back-to-back ascension yet!" Xi Meili said, her voice filled with excitement.
He nodded, "I want to regain my body as soon as possible, after all."
"Your body?" Tan Songyun inquired.
"It's a little complicated, but this body is merely constructed from a part of my soul," he explained. "In order to come to the Nine Heavens with my real body, I need to reach the Seventh Heaven."

chapters.title: Chapter 1762 Five Breakthrough Towers
paragraphs: Sometime after explaining the situation to Tan Songyun, Yuan made his way to the Stairway to Heaven.

However, upon arriving at the Stairway to Heaven, Yuan noticed that there were only a few individuals present, and most of them weren't participants, but spectators gathered to see the participants off.

Since Yuan had entered the Fifth Heaven alone, the rest of the player base was still stuck in the Fourth Heaven. As a result, it was essentially impossible for him to carry nine individuals through the Stairway to Heaven by himself.

Of course, Yuan could attempt to fill the required number with people from the Fifth Heaven, but he would need to find individuals willing to ascend to the Sixth Heaven. Unlike players, who could traverse between realms with ease, ascending was a significant and life-altering decision for residents of the Nine Heavens, not something they could decide on a whim.
'Do I even need to carry people with me? I can just alter the difficulty accordingly!' Yuan just realized this, but he wasn't sure it'd work.
"I'll see you on the other side," Xi Meili said to Yuan.

"Lady Tan, do you want to come with me? Although you have already passed all trials and reached the Ninth Heaven, you can still spectate me. I'm sure you'll learn a thing or two about Tian Kai if you do."
Tan Songyun nodded, "That's only natural. I was going to follow you even if you didn't ask."
Lan Yingying emerged shortly after to follow Xi Meili, as she also wanted to challenge the Stairway to Heaven.
"Who is this?" Tan Songyun asked with raised eyebrows. "And where did she come from?"
"My name is Lan Yingying, and I am a divine beast currently following Yuan."
"Another divine beast?" Tan Songyun muttered with a surprised look on her face.
Having one divine beast as a follower was already rare enough, much less two.
"Why are they following you, anyways?" she then asked out of curiosity.
"They have their own reasons," Yuan shrugged.
Yuan climbed the staircase and entered the Stairway to Heaven shortly after, followed by Tan Songyun.
"Welcome back, Master."
"I don't have nine people with me this time, but is it possible for me to increase the difficulty to the max?" Yuan asked her.
"If that is what you wish, Master."
"Great. Let's do that, then. I would also like to challenge the Stairway to Heaven now."
Tian'er nodded and disappeared shortly later.
Meanwhile, Tan Songyun was examining the spectator's room with great interest.
"I didn't know there was a place like this inside the Stairway to Heaven..."
Since she did everything solo, there was simply no way for her to have known about it.
In the center of the room was a small well filled with water, and reflected on that water was Yuan, who had just begun his first trial.
<You have started your first trial in the Stairway to Heaven>
<Investigate the Five Breakthrough Towers and figure out the one who needs to be punished>
<You have 365 days to complete the trial>
<Figure out the truth and punish the perpetrator within six months to receive a reward>
As Yuan stood in the middle of the bustling street, his eyes widened in surprise as he read the details of the trial's challenge.
'I have a whole year to complete this challenge?' he wondered inwardly.
This officially made it his longest trial yet. Moreover, it appeared more complicated than the previous trials.
However, he wasn't familiar with the Five Breakthrough Towers.
After standing around for a bit, Yuan decided to gather information first.
He approached someone working behind a food stall and asked, "Excuse me, can you tell me a little about the Five Breakthrough Towers?"
The middle-aged woman looked at him with raised eyebrows and spoke, "You don't know about the Five Breakthrough Towers? You're the first person I've met in the Seventh Heaven who doesn't know them."
"Well, I'm not from around here. I just ascended to this realm."
"I see. I don't mind telling you, but..."
The woman extended her hand and gestured for something.
Seeing this, Yuan retrieved some money and handed it to her.
"Thank you, Young Master."
Satisfied by the amount of money, the woman began explaining, "The Five Breakthrough Towers are the most important organizations in the Seventh Heaven."
"Organizations?" Yuan inquired about the specific word.
She nodded. "Yes, they are neither a family, sect, nor faction. They are an organization supported by these groups, each contributing its own unique specialty and purpose."

"The first of the Five Breakthrough Towers is called the Alchemy Tower. They specialize in the study of alchemy and hold the vital role of developing new recipes and refining alchemy techniques," she continued.
"The second tower is called the Array Tower. They specialize in developing new formations and enhancing existing ones."
"The third tower is the Martial Tower. Their primary focus is on creating new martial techniques and refining older ones."
"The fourth tower is the Cultivation Tower. They're similar to the Martial Tower, but they only deal with cultivation techniques."
"The final tower is called the Metal Tower. They not only create treasures, but they study smithing techniques and whatnot."

"If you haven't noticed yet, each of these towers was established with the purpose of advancing a specific path. However, they are entirely separate organizations with no direct association with one another. And because they are all striving for progress in their respective fields, there's a great deal of competition among them."
Yuan was quite amazed by this concept, and he asked, "What are their reputations like?"
"As far as I am aware, they are all very respectable and trustworthy. I don't think I have ever heard anything bad about them," she said.
"Not even rumors? There are always rumors."

The woman pondered for a moment and spoke in a genuine tone, "They say the workers are overly passionate about their job, no matter which tower they belong to, but I wouldn't consider that a bad thing."

chapters.title: Chapter 1763 Metal Tower
paragraphs: Yuan pointed to a tall tower-like building in the distance and asked, "Is that one of these Breakthrough Towers?"
The woman nodded, "Yes, that would be the Metal Tower."
"Where can I find the other towers?"
"They are scattered throughout the Seventh Heaven. Unfortunately, I don't know the exact location of the other towers."
"Is that so? Thank you for the information."

Yuan ended their conversation and made his way toward the Metal Tower. As he approached, he noticed that the entire structure was constructed from shiny black metal, its surface gleaming under the light.
Meanwhile, Tan Songyun wore a pondering expression on her face.

"The Five Breakthrough Towers? Why are they in the Stairway to Heaven? More importantly... what the hell is going on? Did the Stairway to Heaven create such an elaborate world for his trial? I have never heard of anything like this before!"
Suddenly, she sensed a presence behind her. Turning around, she was startled to see a cute child standing there, having appeared silently, almost like a ghost.
"Who are you? And where did you come from?" Tan Songyun asked, as she was certain that nobody else had followed them into the Stairway to Heaven.
"My name is Tian'er, and I have been here since the very beginning, as I am the Stairway to Heaven's spirit," she responded calmly.
"What? The Stairway to Heaven has a spirit?" Tan Songyun's eyes widened at this shocking information.
Tian'er nodded in confirmation and continued, "Master ordered me to help clear up any uncertainty you may have, so here I am."
"Master...?"
"The individual partaking in the trial right now is my Master. He is also the creator of the Stairway to Heaven."

"W-wait a second... Tian Kai created the Stairway to Heaven? That's impossible. The Stairway to Heaven existed long before he even came into existence!" Tan Songyun refuted her claim, using this obvious fact as proof.
"I am not talking about Tian Kai, but an even older reincarnation. Tian Kai is merely one of Master's multiple lives, after all."
"What in heaven's name...?" Tan Songyun was speechless.

However, after some pondering, Tan Songyun realized it wasn't strange for an individual to have reincarnated multiple times. After all, humans naturally reincarnate each time they die, provided the soul remains intact.
'Wait a minute... Can I even trust what she's saying? Tian Kai—Yuan is her Master, so he could easily make her lie...' Tan Songyun thought to herself.
"I heard that it was the God of Creation who created the Stairway to Heaven. Are you telling me that your Master was the God of Creation in one of his previous lives?" Tan Songyun asked.
Tian'er nodded.
"It's not just the Stairway to Heaven. Master has created many things throughout his life, with many of them still undiscovered to this very day."
Tan Songyun swallowed nervously at such implications.
"Then, can you tell me what's going on with his trial? How come it's so different? I know everyone has their own trials, but the disparity isn't this massive." Tan Songyun then inquired.

"For Master, the Stairway to Heaven is not merely a way to travel through the Nine Heavens," Tian'er explained. "It also holds memories of Master's past lives, and the trials help him recover those memories."
"Huh? So what I am looking at right now is actually memories?" Tan Songyun looked at the vast world Yuan was in.
"You're half right," she clarified. "The trials are created from his memories, but they are only fragments pieced together, like parts of a puzzle. They don't directly mirror his actual memories."
After taking a long moment to digest the information given, Tan Songyun asked, "Whose memories am I looking at right now?"
However, Tian'er shook her head and said, "Unfortunately, I cannot answer that."
"Why not? Are you afraid that I might know too much?"
Tian'er shook her head once again and clarified, "No. There are just some things I am not allowed to say. If you really wish to know, you can ask Master later."

Meanwhile, Yuan continued asking several pedestrians about the Metal Tower as he approached his destination. He was particularly curious to know if there were any negative rumors about the place. However, everyone he spoke to praised the Metal Tower, describing its reputation as sparkling clean. While that might seem reassuring on the surface, Yuan couldn't help but become suspicious.
After all, it could all be a facade—a carefully crafted mask to conceal the true evil lurking within. Yet, Yuan had no way to know for sure without visiting the Metal Tower himself.

The Metal Tower appeared close at first glance, but it was actually several days away. Now, standing before it several days later, Yuan realized just how massive it truly was. Not only was the tower so tall that it pierced the clouds, but its interior was vast enough to house a large community of tens of thousands of people simultaneously.
The massive entrance, notably without doors, bustled with a steady stream of people entering and leaving.

After stepping inside the tower, Yuan quickly noticed that the entire first floor resembled a bustling shopping mall, filled with hundreds of stores and even personal stalls offering a wide variety of treasures.
After looking around for some time, Yuan approached one of the merchants and asked, "Excuse me, I am trying to join the Metal Tower. Where can I go to sign up?"
The best way to gain information about a place was to join them, after all.
However, the merchant merely sneered in disguise at Yuan and said, "Who do you think you are? The Metal Tower doesn't just accept anybody."
"I am a blacksmith, and I am very confident in my skills."

"Hahaha! You're truly an ignorant one, aren't you? To make me laugh, I'll tell you something. Talent alone won't get you into the Metal Tower. Unless you know someone on the inside, you'll need to increase your reputation—enough to get the Metal Tower to notice you." The man gestured at the weapons he'd personally crafted before him.
"The fastest way to gain reputation is to showcase your weapons here, just like many of us are doing."

Tian Kai is merely one of Master's multiple lives, after all."
"What in heaven's name...?" Tan Songyun was speechless.
However, after some pondering, Tan Songyun realized it wasn't strange for an individual to have reincarnated multiple times.
After all, humans naturally reincarnate each time they die, provided the soul remains intact.
'Wait a minute...
Can I even trust what she's saying?
Tian Kai—Yuan is her Master, so he could easily make her lie...' Tan Songyun thought to herself.
"I heard that it was the God of Creation who created the Stairway to Heaven.
Are you telling me that your Master was the God of Creation in one of his previous lives?" Tan Songyun asked.
Tian'er nodded.
"It's not just the Stairway to Heaven.
Master has created many things throughout his life, with many of them still undiscovered to this very day."
Tan Songyun swallowed nervously at such implications.
"Then, can you tell me what's going on with his trial?
How come it's so different?
I know everyone has their own trials, but the disparity isn't this massive." Tan Songyun then inquired.
"For Master, the Stairway to Heaven is not merely a way to travel through the Nine Heavens," Tian'er explained.
"It also holds memories of Master's past lives, and the trials help him recover those memories."
"Huh?
So what I am looking at right now is actually memories?" Tan Songyun looked at the vast world Yuan was in.
"You're half right," she clarified.
"The trials are created from his memories, but they are only fragments pieced together, like parts of a puzzle.
They don't directly mirror his actual memories."
After taking a long moment to digest the information given, Tan Songyun asked, "Whose memories am I looking at right now?"
However, Tian'er shook her head and said, "Unfortunately, I cannot answer that."
"Why not?
Are you afraid that I might know too much?"
Tian'er shook her head once again and clarified, "No.
There are just some things I am not allowed to say.
If you really wish to know, you can ask Master later."
Meanwhile, Yuan continued asking several pedestrians about the Metal Tower as he approached his destination.
He was particularly curious to know if there were any negative rumors about the place.
However, everyone he spoke to praised the Metal Tower, describing its reputation as sparkling clean.
While that might seem reassuring on the surface, Yuan couldn't help but become suspicious.
After all, it could all be a facade—a carefully crafted mask to conceal the true evil lurking within.
Yet, Yuan had no way to know for sure without visiting the Metal Tower himself.
The Metal Tower appeared close at first glance, but it was actually several days away.
Now, standing before it several days later, Yuan realized just how massive it truly was.
Not only was the tower so tall that it pierced the clouds, but its interior was vast enough to house a large community of tens of thousands of people simultaneously.
The massive entrance, notably without doors, bustled with a steady stream of people entering and leaving.

After stepping inside the tower, Yuan quickly noticed that the entire first floor resembled a bustling shopping mall, filled with hundreds of stores and even personal stalls offering a wide variety of treasures.
After looking around for some time, Yuan approached one of the merchants and asked, "Excuse me, I am trying to join the Metal Tower.
Where can I go to sign up?"
The best way to gain information about a place was to join them, after all.
However, the merchant merely sneered in disguise at Yuan and said, "Who do you think you are?
The Metal Tower doesn't just accept anybody."
"I am a blacksmith, and I am very confident in my skills."
"Hahaha!
You're truly an ignorant one, aren't you?
To make me laugh, I'll tell you something.
Talent alone won't get you into the Metal Tower.
Unless you know someone on the inside, you'll need to increase your reputation—enough to get the Metal Tower to notice you." The man gestured at the weapons he'd personally crafted before him.
"The fastest way to gain reputation is to showcase your weapons here, just like many of us are doing."

chapters.title: Chapter 1764 Metal Tower(2)
paragraphs: To capture the Metal Tower's attention, most blacksmiths showcase their creations on the tower's first floor, which also serves as an open marketplace. However, despite the abundance of talented blacksmiths, only about ten individuals gain the Metal Tower's recognition every few hundred years.

"I've been selling my creations here for about a hundred years now," the man said. "In all that time, I've only seen three people be recognized by the Metal Tower. But let me tell you, being recognized doesn't mean you'll be accepted—that's an entirely different matter."
"I see. Thank you for the information," Yuan said to the man.
He left shortly after and began roaming the first floor, examining all of the stores available.

Now that Yuan understood how to attract the Metal Tower's attention, he knew he needed to craft treasures that would quickly build his reputation. The simplest and most effective way to achieve this was to create something far superior to anything else being showcased around him.

After exploring every store on the first floor, Yuan observed that most of the treasures on display were only Ancient-grade, with a few Mythic-grade items scattered among them. However, even the Mythic-grade treasures were of noticeably low quality.
'A few peak-quality Mythic-grade and Empyrean-grade treasures should be more than enough to attract the Metal Tower's attention.' Yuan thought to himself as he left the Metal Tower.
Thanks to the Metal Tower's influence, the area surrounding it was teeming with smithies and smithing-related stores, including shops selling various materials and tools essential for crafting.
Yuan entered a nearby smithy and requested to use their workshop.
"Hello, I would like to borrow the workshop to create some treasures."
The bulky man standing behind the counter looked at Yuan like he was crazy.
"You got any identification? A blacksmith identification, to be more specific."
"Sorry, but I don't have anything like that."
"Then we cannot lend you our workshop, no matter how much you offer. If you wish to use our workshop, you need to be an official blacksmith."
"How do I become an official blacksmith?" Yuan asked.
"Hahaha! You want to become an official blacksmith, but you don't even know how? You're an amusing one!" The bulky man laughed out loud.
He continued, "Ten blocks down, there is a place called the Blacksmith Association. In order to be recognized as an official blacksmith, you must pass several tests."
"Thank you. Then I will be back after I acquire my identification," Yuan said to the man.
"Hahaha! If a scrawny kid like you can pass the assessment, I'll gladly let you use my workshop for free!"
"Scrawny?" Yuan raised an eyebrow. This was the first time he had ever been referred to with such a term.

Yuan's physique might appear scrawny compared to the bulky man standing before him, but in reality, it was perfectly balanced and refined to an unparalleled degree of perfection, being neither too skinny nor too bulky.

Yuan left the store shortly after, but he didn't immediately head to the Blacksmith Association. Instead, he decided to try his luck at a few more smithies. Unfortunately, all of them required him to be an official blacksmith.
'I guess this is a process I must go through to progress the trial.' Yuan thought to himself as he visited the Blacksmith Association.
The Blacksmith Association was an enormous building spanning several streets, its reflective surface and metallic structure giving it the appearance of a solid block of steel at first glance.
Yuan walked inside the building and approached the nearest worker.
"I'd like to take the assessment to become an official blacksmith."
The worker, a young man, nodded, "Sure thing. May I ask how experienced you are with the art?"
"I'd say that I'm quite experienced."
"Then what is the highest grade of treasure you've created?"
"Celestial-grade." Yuan calmly responded.
The young man's eyes immediately widened with disbelief. He didn't respond for several moments due to being speechless.
Eventually, he said, "That's a good joke, but I need a serious answer."
Yuan's expression remained calm as he responded, "I am dead serious."

Seeing Yuan's solemn gaze, the young man swallowed nervously and spoke in a stiff voice, "T-then will you be fine with accepting the most difficult assessment? If you pass, we'll grant you the highest Blacksmith Rank we can possibly give you. Even if you fail, you can try again with a lower difficulty."
Yuan nodded, "Sure, give me your most difficult assessment."
The young man nodded and said, "Please give me a moment to notify my superiors."
Sometime later, an old man with long, short white hair and a curly mustache approached Yuan and asked, "Are you the one who requested our most difficult assessment?"
Yuan nodded.
"Follow me."
Yuan followed the old man to the basement, where a large workshop was available.

"Since you claim to be able to craft Celestial-grade treasures, we'll have you craft an Empyrean-grade treasure for your assessment. If you are able to do so, the Blacksmith Association will immediately promote you to our highest blacksmith rank," said the old man.
Yuan pondered for a moment before asking, "Does the Blacksmith Association have any connections with the Metal Tower?"

The old man quickly understood what Yuan was trying to ask and said, "While we do have some connections and can recommend you to the Metal Tower, it is up to them whether they are willing to accept you. Moreover, Divine Blacksmiths are not rare in the Metal Tower, so even if you are capable of crafting Celestial-grade treasures, it won't guarantee you a spot in the Metal Tower."
"I see. Thanks for the explanation."
The old man retrieved a pile of materials a moment later and said, "You have three months to craft the treasure using the materials we provide you. Are you ready to begin?"
"I am ready."
Yuan spent a couple of minutes examining the materials. Once he was prepared, he immediately began to work.

Less than a day later, Yuan presented his finished creation to the old man, who was utterly gobsmacked, not only by the masterpiece itself but also by the sheer brilliance of the process that had brought it to life.

chapters.title: Chapter 1765 Metal Tower(3)
paragraphs: "What do you think? Did I pass the assessment?" Yuan asked the dumbfounded old man, who was staring at the finished treasure with wide eyes filled with disbelief.
Although smithing had advanced significantly since Tian Qiyuan's era, with the emergence of many more Divine Blacksmiths, Tian Qiyuan's smithing skills remained unparalleled.
"C-can I examine the treasure?" the old man asked.
Yuan nodded and handed the sword to him.
The old man held the sword in his trembling hands, feeling as though he were cradling a priceless treasure of unimaginable value.
"I have never seen an Empyrean-grade treasure of this quality before!" he muttered.

"Pass! You pass! Congratulations, you are now officially an Obisidian-rank blacksmith!" The old man handed Yuan a black badge, its surface gleaming with understated elegance. This badge held immense significance in the world of blacksmiths, representing the pinnacle of achievement. Within the Blacksmith Association, there were six ranks that could be obtained, with Obsidian—the rank represented by this badge—being the highest and most revered.

Normally, becoming an Obsidian-ranked blacksmith required passing multiple rigorous assessments. However, Yuan's flawless performance in his first trial was so extraordinary that the remaining tests were deemed redundant and unnecessary by the old man, who was also a Divine Blacksmith.

"I haven't introduced myself yet. I am the head of the Blacksmith Association, Lie Yan. If you ever need any assistance from the Blacksmith Association, we will always be there to help you," said the old man.
Yuan nodded and asked, "Do you think I can borrow some materials? I would like to craft a few more treasures."

"Of course! All official blacksmiths under the Blacksmith Association are entitled to a specific allotment of materials every ten years as a privilege," Lie Yan explained. "As an Obsidian-ranked blacksmith, you have near unlimited access to most of our materials, provided the amount you request is reasonable."
"I don't need much. Just enough to craft several Mythic-grade treasures. Also, do I get to keep that sword?" Yuan pointed at the treasure he'd crafted for the assessment.
Lie Yan, seemingly reluctant to let the treasure go, said, "O-of course."
Sometime later, Lie Yan left to acquire the materials Yuan had requested.

Once Lie Yan returned with the materials, he hesitated for a moment before asking, "May I boldly request to watch you work? Even as a Divine Blacksmith, I feel my skills improve simply by observing your craftsmanship."
"Do as you wish," Yuan said.
Yuan proceeded to use almost all of his materials to craft five peak-quality Mythic-grade treasures.
"Thank you for the experience." Lie Yan bowed to Yuan.
"Then I'll take my leave now."

"One more thing before you leave. Although I cannot help you join the Metal Tower, I know some people there. I'll mention your name the next time I visit them. Hopefully, that will help you a little," said Lie Yan.
"Thanks."
Yuan left the Blacksmith Association shortly afterward. However, instead of heading directly back to the Metal Tower, he made his way to the shop with the bulky man.
Once there, Yuan casually revealed his Obsidian badge. The man's jaw practically hit the floor, his eyes wide with disbelief as he stared at the badge in stunned silence.
"Do I qualify to use your workshop?" he asked.
After snapping out of his daze, the man said, "O-of course! You can even have my whole shop if you want!"
Yuan merely shook his head with a slight smile on his face.
The man led Yuan to his workshop at the back of the shop a moment later.

Once inside, Yuan set to work, using the materials he had purposely saved for this occasion. Within a few hours, he had crafted a flawless Mythic-grade treasure, leaving the bulky man utterly speechless as he stared in awe at the masterpiece before him.
"Thanks for lending me the place."
"You can come back here to borrow my workshop whenever you want, Senior! It will always be available for you!"
With his six finished treasures, Yuan returned to the Metal Tower to set up his showcase.
"Oh? You're back already?"
The man who called Yuan ignorant was surprised to see Yuan return so soon. It'd only been a day since their conversation, after all.
"Yes. I took your advice and went to craft some treasures. Do you mind if I set up my showcase next to yours?" Yuan said.

"Hahaha! You've only been gone for a little over a day!" the man laughed, shaking his head. "There's no way whatever you created in such a short time would attract the Metal Tower's attention! Each of my treasures required months, if not years, of hard work!"
"Maybe that's why you haven't gotten the tower's attention." Yuan shrugged.
The man frowned and cursed, "You cheeky bastard!"

Yuan said nothing more and began setting up his spot. He spread a simple blanket on the floor and casually placed the six treasures he had crafted onto it, treating them as if they were mere toys rather than extraordinary creations.
The man's eyes widened with shock after seeing the five Mythic-grade and one Empyrean-grade treasure.
"Y-you crafted that in one day?! That's impossible! You clearly purchased these treasures!" the man screamed out loud, attracting the attention of those nearby.
"That's quite the accusation," Yuan said.
"Anyone with a working brain knows that isn't possible! Even a Divine Blacksmith wouldn't be able to craft six treasures of such quality in a day!"
"Guess I am just different." Yuan casually shrugged.
The man gritted his teeth in frustration.
"This is blasphemy! You're a disgrace! I bet you're not even a blacksmith!"
"Now you're just slandering me. Do you have proof that I didn't craft these treasures? How do you know that I didn't craft them prior to our last conversation?"
"T-that's... Right! If you had these treasures from the start, you would've shown them during that day! Why did you leave for a day?!"
"I was hungry, so I went to eat some food," Yuan said, leaving the man speechless.

chapters.title: Chapter 1766 Metal Tower(4)
paragraphs: Noticing the commotion between Yuan and the man, the nearby blacksmiths eventually approached them and asked, "What's going on here?"

"This bastard here is mocking us, blacksmiths! Listen to this—" the man proceeded to explain the whole situation to the others. Naturally, he spoke from his point of view, labeling Yuan as the bad guy.
"He most likely purchased those treasures from somewhere."

The blacksmiths frowned deeply as they learned of Yuan's actions. Most of them were Platinum-ranked blacksmiths, seasoned and proud of their craft. Yuan's actions were enough to provoke any blacksmith, let alone ones of their caliber—if they were true.
Seeing this, Yuan retrieved his Obsidian-rank badge and shoved it before them.

"T-that's an Obsidian badge!" the man stammered, his voice shaking with disbelief. "Only Divine Blacksmiths can qualify for that rank! Y-you're a Divine Blacksmith?! Why didn't you say so?!" His face, which had been full of scorn just moments ago, now bore a mix of shock and awe as he gazed at the badge that symbolized the rank he had long dreamed of achieving.
"Why didn't I say so? Why must I disclose such information to you when I'm trying to attract the Metal Tower's attention? Who do you think you are?" Yuan sneered.
The man's jaw dropped, speechless.

"Now that I have cleared up the misunderstanding, why don't we all return to our objective—acquiring the Metal Tower's attention?" Yuan sat behind his display and closed his eyes, seemingly entering cultivation.
The blacksmiths there looked at each other. After a moment of silence, they turned around and returned to their own spots.
The man beside Yuan quietly sat down and lowered his head, doing his best to avoid drawing any attention from Yuan, as if trying to make himself invisible.

Yuan's display quickly drew the attention of not only the shoppers but also the other blacksmiths on the first floor of the tower. In no time, a curious and growing crowd had gathered around his setup, intrigued by the treasures he had laid out.
"Do these beautiful treasures have names?" one curious shopper asked.
"No, they do not have a name."
"How long did it take you to craft such masterpieces?" one blacksmith asked.
"The Empyrean-grade treasure took about half a day, and the others only took several hours... in total."
"What?!" The blacksmiths exclaimed, looking like they'd just witnessed a ghost.

The crowd found it hard to believe that someone could craft six flawless treasures in a single day. However, the blacksmiths had already heard about Yuan's status as an Obsidian-ranked blacksmith, so they didn't dare to voice any doubts.
"What?!" The blacksmiths exclaimed, looking like they'd just witnessed a ghost.

The crowd found it hard to believe that someone could craft six flawless treasures in a single day. However, the blacksmiths had already heard about Yuan's status as an Obsidian-ranked blacksmith, so they didn't dare to voice any doubts.
"Umm... Are any of these treasures for sale?" someone suddenly asked.

While most blacksmiths came to the tower not only to showcase their treasures but also to sell them, Yuan had no such intention. He had no need to sell his creations; his sole purpose was to use them as a means to attract the Metal Tower's attention.
After several days of sitting idly with no noticeable change, a sudden commotion erupted on the first floor, breaking the monotony and drawing everyone's attention.
"Someone from the Metal Tower is here, looking around! This is our chance!"
Upon hearing that someone from the tower had arrived, the blacksmiths immediately began tidying up their showcases, frantically trying to make their displays more presentable and impressive.
Meanwhile, Yuan remained seated, his eyes closed and his demeanor calm, as though the news held no significance to him.
At the same time, a handsome young man strolled through the first floor, dressed in an elegant black outfit adorned with a golden badge on his chest that read 'Metal'.

Everywhere he walked, people around him offered respectful stares, their admiration evident. The blacksmiths, in particular, had eyes that gleamed with hope and desperation, eager to catch even a moment of his attention.
Yet, not a single blacksmith dared to approach him, almost as if he was out of their reach.
The handsome man didn't stop walking until he was standing right before Yuan's display.
"Are you the one who recently became an Obsidian-rank blacksmith?" the young man asked.
"And you must be Lie Yan's friend."

The handsome man's eyebrows twitched slightly at Yuan's casual response, a hint of offense flashing across his face. He glanced at the weapons on display, his gaze lingering only briefly—just a fraction longer than a passing look—before sneering, "What a waste of time. chapters.title: Chapter 1767 A Chance of Redemption
paragraphs: After putting away Number One Under Heaven, Yuan continued walking toward the exit.
Seeing this, the handsome man snapped out of his daze and shouted, "Halt!"

However, Yuan kept on walking, and he spoke as he walked, "Who do you think you are to stop me from leaving? You already said my treasures are not worth the Metal Tower's attention, so why would I continue wasting time here? Let's not waste each other's time."
The handsome man trembled with anger, but he couldn't bring himself to utter another word. Saying anything further would be tantamount to admitting his own fault and misjudgment.
Therefore, the handsome man and the others could only watch as Yuan nonchalantly left the Metal Tower.
"He actually left..." the man who had been stationed next to Yuan muttered in a dazed tone, his face frozen in a dumbfounded expression.

A few moments after Yuan departed from the Metal Tower, before the handsome man and the others could fully process what had just occurred, another figure appeared. It was an old man with a bald head, dressed in an outfit similar to the one worn by the handsome man.
"That presence just now! Where is it?! Where did it go?!" the old man bellowed, his voice commanding and urgent, instantly grabbing everyone's attention.
"S-Senior Liao! What brings you down here?" the handsome man exclaimed, a look of genuine surprise spreading across his face as he caught sight of the old man.
However, the old man, Senior Liao, ignored his question and asked again, "The presence that appeared just now! Where did it go?! Where is the treasure that emitted such presence?!"
"T-that's..." the handsome man stammered, swallowing nervously as he hesitated, unsure whether to reveal the truth.
"What are you hiding from me, Apprentice Huan?" Senior Liao frowned.
The handsome man sighed and said, "I wouldn't dare, Senior Liao. This is what happened..."
He recounted the events to Senior Liao, detailing everything that had occurred. However, he carefully omitted certain details—most notably, the reason Yuan had decided to leave.

Unfortunately for him, Senior Liao was not something easily fooled. He narrowed his eyes at Apprentice Huan and said in a cold voice, "Apprentice Huan, I accepted you because of your potential, but I am beginning to doubt my own judgment. I will give you a chance to redeem yourself. Bring that person you chased away back to the Metal Tower. If you cannot do even that, you no longer need to return to the Metal Tower."
"S-Senior Liao?!" Apprentice Huan's face contorted in despair, his expression twisting into something almost unrecognizable.
Having only joined the Metal Tower a decade ago, if he were kicked out over something as seemingly trivial as this, he'd become a laughingstock among his peers and ruin his reputation entirely.
"I will not repeat myself. You have one month to bring him back." Senior Liao turned around and walked away, leaving Apprentice Huan and the others speechless.

Snapping out of his daze a moment later, Apprentice Huan turned toward the exit of the tower. Without hesitation, he rushed outside, determined to find Yuan and convince him to return to the Metal Tower.
Although it hadn't been long since Yuan left the Metal Tower, his figure was nowhere to be seen.

"Fuck! Where did he go?! Did he really leave to another tower?!" Apprentice Huan stomped his feet in frustration. He didn't want to travel to the other towers, but there was nothing he could do, as his future and reputation depended on it.
Meanwhile, after leaving the Metal Tower, Yuan immediately went to the nearest teleport formation.
"I'd like to visit the other Breakthrough Towers," he said to the individual managing the teleportation formation.
"Which one?" "I will let you pick."
"Okay...?"
Sometime later, Yuan stepped into the teleportation formation.

When he emerged on the other side, he found himself in a different city. Turning his gaze toward the skyline, he saw a massive tower in the distance. While it was just as majestic as the Metal Tower, its design and structure were distinctly different. This tower resembled a towering pagoda, exuding an air of elegance and tradition.
Yuan looked at the man managing the teleport formation and asked, "Which Breakthrough Tower is that?"
"Huh?" Although the man was puzzled by such a weird question, he answered regardless, "That would be the Martial Tower."
"Is that so?"
Yuan approached the tower.

Unlike the bustling and open atmosphere of the Metal Tower, the Martial Tower exuded a sense of exclusivity and focus. Its entrance was closed, yet thousands of people had gathered outside, their attention fixed on five large jade tablets prominently displayed near the tower. The crowd buzzed with intensity, their gazes locked on the tablets as though they held immense significance.
Yuan picked a jade tablet at random and looked at the contents written on it.
"It's a martial technique..." It didn't take long for Yuan to realize what he was looking at.

Each jade tablet showcased a martial technique of a different rank engraved onto its surface. The first tablet displayed a Mortal-rank technique, the second an Earth-rank technique, and so on, progressing through the ranks until the highest, an Ancient-rank technique, was reached.
After looking through all five martial techniques, Yuan looked around until he found someone who wasn't completely focused on the techniques and approached them.
"Excuse me, but what is the purpose of these jade tablets?"

The woman he approached looked at him with raised eyebrows and said, "If you can improve any of the martial techniques on the jade tablet and achieve a satisfactory result, the Martial Tower will accept you into their organization."

Yuan understood the situation immediately, but he continued asking, "Why are they all of different ranks? There's even a Mortal-rank technique, which is obviously going to be the easiest to improve. Wouldn't it be fairer if all of the techniques were of the same rank?"
"That's simple," she explained. "The more difficult the challenge you take on, the higher your position within the organization will be if you succeed."
"That makes sense. Thank you for your time and explanation."
Yuan returned to focusing on the martial techniques shortly after.

chapters.title: Chapter 1768 Martial Tower
paragraphs: To improve a martial technique, one must first learn and master it. For Yuan, who had lived multiple lives as powerful immortals, each reigning supreme in their respective eras, this process came naturally. His vast experience with countless techniques made him exceptionally adept in this domain.

After spending a few hours carefully studying the jade tablet with the Ancient-rank technique, Yuan fully grasped it. He then spent the rest of the day with his eyes closed, mentally practicing the martial technique as if he were crafting a treasure within his mind, refining every detail and perfecting it in his imagination.
If it weren't for a disturbance, he would've spent some more time inside his mind.
"You! I've finally found you!" Apprentice Huan shouted when he noticed Yuan amongst the crowd.
Due to Yuan's handsome features, he stuck out like a sore thumb no matter how big the crowd around him was.

After leaving the Metal Tower, Apprentice Huan spent several hours scouring the city in search of Yuan. Eventually, he decided to check the teleportation formation, hoping for a lead. Sure enough, the attendant working the formation remembered Yuan and confirmed that he had used it recently.
Yuan frowned after seeing Apprentice Huan and said, "Don't tell me you followed me all the way here?"
"I had no choice! You must return to the Metal Tower with me as soon as possible! Senior Liao wants to see you!" Apprentice Huan said, not even bothering to apologize.
"Senior who?" Yuan raised an eyebrow at this unfamiliar name.
"You don't even know the Master of the Metal Tower, Liao Tian?! He once held the title of God of Creation before retiring!" Apprentice Huan exclaimed, his face filled with disbelief.
Yuan shrugged nonchalantly, "Thanks for the introduction. I definitely didn't know him before it."
"Y-you disrespectful son—" Apprentice Huan forcefully stopped himself from finishing the sentence.
"Now you know who's summoned you, follow me back to the Metal Tower."

However, Yuan sneered, "So what if he was once the God of Creation? Even if he were the current God of Creation, I don't care! If he wants me to return to the Metal Tower, he better invite me in person!"
"You're going too far, bastard!" Apprentice Huan roared.

"I'm going too far? You were the one who drove me away, and instead of apologizing, you're still looking down on me. Unless this Liao Tian visits me personally, I won't return to the Metal Tower until I visit the other four Breakthrough Towers!" Yuan declared, leaving Apprentice Huan speechless.
After a moment of silence, he trembled in anger and screamed, "Either you follow me back willingly, or I will force you to go back!"
"Oh? I'd love to see you try."
Yuan beckoned Apprentice Huan. This was the perfect time for him to improve the Ancient-rank technique through practical use.
Apprentice Huan sneered in disdain and released his cultivation base, which was at the first level of Divine Ancestor.

'Senior Liao only mentioned bringing him back to the Metal Tower! He didn't say in what condition! I'll drag him back even if it's only his corpse!' Apprentice Huan laughed inwardly, showing a menacing expression on his face.
Seeing that two experts were about to clash, the people there immediately scrambled to safety.
Yuan retrieved his Baneful Abyss, as the Ancient-rank technique was a dagger technique.
'Since this is the Stairway to Heaven's trial, I don't have to worry about killing innocent people with its powerful poison.'
Apprentice Huan trembled in fear after sensing the Baneful Abyss' ominous aura.
"Did you create that monstrosity?" Apprentice Huan asked with a deep frown. "Where are your morals?"
"Morals? I'm surprised you can even utter such a word!" Yuan laughed out loud.
He then shouted out loud, "Martial Tower, are you watching this right now?! I will now display my improvements for the Ancient-rank martial technique!"
Yuan pointed the Banefull Abyss at Apprentice Huan and said, "Don't worry, I won't kill you. After all, how else will you tell Liao Tian to come find me?"
"Arrogant son of a bitch!"
Just as Apprentice Huan leaped forward, Yuan's aura exploded after activating True Dragon Awakening.
The abrupt appearance of such powerful pressure startled Apprentice Huan, causing him to hesitate for a split second.
Yuan used this opportunity to attack.
A black streak of light appeared, piercing Apprentice Huan's left arm faster than one could blink their eyes.
"Wha—"

Before Apprentice Huan could even process what was happening, an intense pain suddenly engulfed his entire body. It felt as though his insides were melting, the agony so overwhelming that it left him gasping for breath and unable to think clearly.
If Apprentice Huan's cultivation weren't at the Divine Ancestor realm, he would've perished the second Baneful Abyss touched him.
As Apprentice Huan rolled on the ground, screaming in pain, Yuan approached him.
Right before Apprentice Huan succumbed to the poison, Yuan removed the poison.
"Go back to Liao Tian and tell him to see me personally if he wants me to return to the Metal Tower," he said a moment later.

A deafening silence enveloped the area as the onlookers stood frozen in disbelief. They couldn't fathom how easily Yuan had defeated someone several cultivation realms stronger than himself, executing the feat with such effortless grace.
"Hahaha!"
An amused laugh suddenly shattered the silence.

When Yuan and the others turned toward the source of the laughter, they saw a wise-looking old man standing before them, his presence so sudden and silent it was as if he had materialized like a ghost.
"Y-you are—!" Apprentice Huan instantly recognized this old man, as did the other onlookers.
"Lord Zi!" Everyone except Yuan immediately lowered their heads in respect toward the old man, whose aura and demeanor made it clear that he was a figure of immense significance.

Without even looking at Apprentice Huan, the old man faced Yuan and spoke with a smile on his face, "That was magnificent—your improvement to that martial technique. How long did it take you to come up with something like that?"
"A little under a day. If I hadn't been interrupted by someone, I could've improved it even further," he replied.
The old man's eyes widened.

paragraphs: "I see... so it only took you a day to improve an Ancient-rank technique. Your wisdom and talent is very impressive. How about joining our Martial Tower? Let us usher martial techniques into a new era together!" said Lord Zi.
Yuan then said, "I can join the Martial Tower, but will I be allowed to visit the other Breakthrough Towers afterward?"

Lord Zi nodded, "Of course. While we are very competitive with each other, we all have similar goals and ambitions. We won't bar you from joining other towers just because you are associated with another tower."
"In that case, I'll join the Martial Tower."
"Hahaha! Great choice, my young friend! Follow me. I'll give you a tour around the place."
Yuan nodded and followed Lord Zi into the tower. Meanwhile, Apprentice Huan remained standing outside the Martial Tower with a perplexed expression on his face.
On one hand, he couldn't return to the Metal Tower without Yuan. On the other, he couldn't approach Yuan with Lord Zi beside him.
Lord Zi was not just a member of the Martial Tower. His status was akin to Liao Tian in the Metal Tower, with a significant amount of achievements under his belt.

Upon stepping onto the first floor of the Martial Tower, Yuan was greeted by a scene reminiscent of a bustling training ground. Numerous individuals were scattered throughout, diligently practicing martial techniques and honing their skills.

"The first ten floors of the tower are essentially the same," Lord Zi explained. "The Martial Tower isn't just about improving martial techniques—we also create and record them. Of course, we only have access to techniques that are entrusted to us. When we started, our resources were scarce, with barely any techniques to work with. But over time, as we proved ourselves by refining and enhancing techniques, more and more people began trusting us with their precious techniques."
At the end of the room was a teleportation formation that provided access to the upper floors. Since the first ten floors were essentially identical, they proceeded directly to the eleventh floor.

Unlike the bustling training ground on the first floor, the eleventh floor resembled a vast library. Shelves lined the walls, filled with scrolls and books, and many individuals were seated, deeply engrossed in studying martial techniques.

"The next ten floors are like this," Lord Zi said as they walked around the place. "We house martial techniques ranging from Mortal-rank to Celestial-rank. However, only a select few individuals are permitted to study techniques above Supreme-rank. All of the techniques on this floor are merely Mortal-rank.

"Everyone starts from Mortal-rank techniques. In order to study the next rank, they must increase their contribution, which can be gained through improving or creating martial techniques. For example, improving a Mortal-rank technique will gain one contribution point, while creating a Mortal-rank technique will grant ten points."

"The next ten floors are like this," Lord Zi said as they walked around the place. "We house martial techniques ranging from Mortal-rank to Celestial-rank. However, only a select few individuals are permitted to study techniques above Supreme-rank. All of the techniques on this floor are merely Mortal-rank."

"Everyone starts from Mortal-rank techniques. In order to study the next rank, they must increase their contribution, which can be gained through improving or creating martial techniques. For example, improving a Mortal-rank technique will gain one contribution point, while creating a Mortal-rank technique will grant ten points."
"Since you've already improved an Ancient-rank technique, you'll automatically be allowed to study martial techniques up to Ancient-rank techniques."
Next, they proceeded directly to the twenty-first floor. Unlike the previous floors, this one featured only a few rooms, each with a closed door.
"These are seclusion chambers," Lord Zi explained. "They're reserved for individuals working on creating new martial techniques."
"Let me show you how they work."

They entered an unoccupied room, and to Yuan's surprise, the interior was completely bare, devoid of any furniture or decorations. The emptiness was stark and unexpected. However, upon closer inspection, Yuan noticed the room was actually filled with powerful formations.
"I know what you're thinking. How can someone create martial techniques in such a boring environment?"

Creating martial techniques was a challenging and intricate process. There were several approaches to it, with the most common being drawing inspiration from one's surroundings or observing others in combat. Some even derived martial techniques from nature—studying the movements of an insect walking, a bird flying, or the flow of water in a stream could spark the creation of a new technique.
"There are multiple formations inside this room, which can be used to do this—"

Lord Zi closed his eyes, and moments later, the empty room began to shift and change. The surroundings transformed, and they found themselves standing at the edge of a towering cliff overlooking a vast, endless ocean. The sound of crashing waves and the scent of salty air filled the space, making the illusion feel incredibly real.

The scenery shifted once more a few moments later, and they now found themselves witnessing a breathtaking battle between two powerful cultivators in the starry sky. The clash of their techniques lit up the cosmos, each strike rippling through the heavens with unimaginable force.
"The only limitation is your imagination," said Lord Zi.

Once they left the room, Lord Zi said, "This is the furthest I can take you inside the Martial Tower. Here is your Martial Tower badge, which can be used as a storage ring and a communication jade slip. You can also see which floors you have access to inside."
"In order to gain more access, I need to contribute to the Martial Tower, correct?" Yuan asked.
Lord Zi nodded.
"What gives the most contribution points?"
Lord Zi chuckled and said, "I like your enthusiasm, but it takes time to reach the top. However, if you can create a Mythic-rank technique, I'll consider giving you a quick promotion to the top."
"A Mythic-rank technique, huh?" Yuan mumbled.

Even with his vast experience throughout multiple lifetimes, it wasn't easy to create a Mythic-rank technique on the spot. The martial techniques he had made before all required hundreds, if not thousands, of years. Of course, they were all top martial techniques amongst their ranks.
"Alright, then I will immediately start," Yuan said a moment later.

"Sure thing. Now that you are a member of the Martial Tower, you're free to do as you please. If you ever need help with anything, you can speak with the others." Lord Zi said to him before leaving him alone.
Yuan returned to the room shortly after.

chapters.title: Chapter 1770 Creating a New Martial Technique
paragraphs: After returning to the seclusion chamber, Yuan sat down and closed his eyes, entering a state of deep contemplation about the martial technique he intended to create.

Unlike crafting treasures of specific ranks, creating a martial technique was far more unpredictable and perplexing. Even if Yuan aimed to create a Mythic-rank technique, there was no guarantee it would achieve that rank. It could just as easily result in an Ancient-rank technique or even something of lower rank, depending on the execution and refinement of his concept.

However, there was a method to increase the likelihood of creating martial techniques of a specific rank— by combining two or more techniques of that rank. By merging their principles and mechanics, one could craft a new, often more powerful, technique that retained the essence of its predecessors while pushing beyond its original limitations.

For instance, Yuan could attempt to merge two Mythic-rank techniques together to create a superior technique. However, while the concept sounded simple, it was far more difficult to achieve in practice, as the techniques needed to be compatible with each other. Even a minor incompatibility could cause the fusion to fail or result in a broken technique.

After several hours of deep contemplation, Yuan decided to attempt creating a combination technique using Nine Supreme Swords and Asura's Blade of Execution, two exceptionally powerful Mythic-rank techniques.
Not only did Yuan possess complete mastery and understanding of both techniques, but their foundations were remarkably similar, making them ideal candidates for fusion.

Nine Supreme Swords focused on overwhelming and dominating its target through relentless and precise strikes, whereas Asura's Blade of Execution was designed purely for lethal efficiency, delivering swift and decisive killing blows.

If he successfully combined the two techniques, Yuan would create a martial technique capable of unleashing immense destruction—one that could dominate and annihilate targets with unparalleled precision and lethal force.

Using his imagination and the unique capabilities of the seclusion chamber, Yuan began visualizing the combination of the two techniques. The formations within the chamber responded to his thoughts, creating an illusion that vividly demonstrated the potential outcome of combining Nine Supreme Swords and Asura's Blade of Execution.
However, Yuan didn't stop there and tried several variations of the technique until he was satisfied with the results.
As Yuan became deeply engrossed in the process of creating his new technique, time seemed to blur, and before he realized it, nearly an entire month had passed in the blink of an eye.
After using the formation to demonstrate the technique one last time, Yuan left the seclusion chamber with a satisfied smile on his face.
Then, he used the Martial Tower's badge to contact Lord Zi. Unfortunately, due to a lack of authority, Yuan could only send a message to Lord Zi and wait for a response.
While he waited for Lord Zi to respond, Yuan visited the lower floors, specifically the twenty-seventh floor, which contained mostly Ancient-rank techniques.

When Yuan arrived at the twenty-seventh floor, he noticed a stark contrast in the number of people present. Unlike the bustling twenty-first floor, which was crowded with hundreds of individuals, this floor had only about a dozen people scattered throughout.

The number of available techniques on the twenty-seventh floor was also significantly lower. While the twenty-first floor boasted tens of thousands of techniques filling tall shelves, the twenty-seventh floor had only about a hundred Ancient-rank techniques carefully arranged.
Yuan proceeded to take a look at these techniques. Naturally, he had no plans of improving them and only wanted to learn some new techniques.
'Since this place was created by the Stairway to Heaven, these techniques are mine to begin with.'
After looking through several techniques, Yuan realized that most of them were martial techniques meant for daggers, almost as if it was implying something.
'This trial must be related to Tian Kai...'
Although he already had such suspicions, he wasn't certain until he saw these techniques.
Several hours later, Yuan's Martial Tower badge trembled, indicating that someone was trying to contact him.
"Come to the tenth floor. I'll be there in five minutes," Lord Zi's voice echoed.

Hearing this, Yuan promptly made his way to the tenth floor. Expecting to find a few people training, he was surprised to discover the floor completely empty, with not a single soul present besides himself.
Lord Zi showed up a few minutes later, but there was a solemn expression on his face.
"You better not be messing with me when you said that you have finished creating a new Mythic-rank martial technique. It hasn't even been a month since our last conversation, after all."
Yuan smiled and said, "Don't worry, I wouldn't dare to lie."

Lord Zi narrowed his eyes as he studied Yuan. Having spent tens of thousands of years with the Martial Tower and personally creating dozens of Mythic-rank techniques, he fully understood the immense difficulty and time required to achieve such a feat. Yet, in all his centuries of experience, he had never encountered or even heard of anyone crafting a Mythic-rank technique in such an astoundingly short period of time.

"I will give you one chance to double-check your creation," Lord Zi said, his expression grim and his tone severe. "If it turns out that you've wasted my time, I will expel you from the Martial Tower immediately. I have no tolerance for those who carelessly create techniques."
Hearing such words, Yuan merely nodded in silence.
"Good. Then attack me with your new technique. Do not worry about hurting me." Lord Zi unleashed his aura, revealing his cultivation to be in the Golden Immortal Realm.
Yuan immediately began demonstrating his newly created technique, and as he did so, his killing intent surged to an overwhelming level, catching Lord Zi off guard.

Suddenly, an avatar resembling God of War's Astral Arts appeared above Lord Zi. It carried a massive sword in one hand and an equally imposing dagger in the other. The sword radiated a domineering aura, exuding an overwhelming power that seemed capable of destroying everything in its path. At the same time, the dagger emanated an intense killing intent so profound it felt as though it could annihilate all life in an instant. The sheer presence of the technique was suffocating, leaving Lord Zi in stunned silence.

chapters.title: Chapter 1771 God of War’s Final Execution
paragraphs: "W-what a terrifying technique..." Lord Zi muttered, his voice trembling as he stared at the avatar. He could feel an overwhelming sense of dread emanating from it, his entire being shuddering in a mixture of fear and awe.
Although Yuan had initially intended to combine only Nine Supreme Swords and Asura's Blade of Execution, he found himself incorporating elements of God of War's Astral Arts into the mix.
"I call this technique... God of War's Final Execution."
Yuan made a subtle gesture, and in response, the avatar above Lord Zi raised both its arms. Without hesitation, it began slashing with its sword and stabbing with its dagger in a relentless assault.

Lord Zi enveloped his body in Immortal Qi, bracing himself as he raised his arms to block the incoming strikes. While he initially managed to deflect the first few attacks with relative ease, he soon noticed that each successive strike grew more powerful and increasingly difficult to withstand.

While the Nine Supreme Swords concluded with nine devastating strikes, God of War's Final Execution followed an entirely different principle. The technique was relentless, continuing its assault until its target was utterly obliterated.

What made it even more terrifying was its escalating power—each strike growing stronger than the last. However, this came at a significant cost, as every attack drained Yuan's spiritual energy. Moreover, the energy expenditure increased alongside the technique's growing strength, meaning the longer it lasted, the more difficult it became for Yuan to sustain.
At Yuan's current cultivation level, even if he could recover his spiritual energy in the blink of an eye, it wouldn't matter if a single strike demanded more energy than he could supply.
In the end, Yuan managed to execute God of War's Final Execution 20 times, cutting through approximately 60 percent of Lord Zi's Immortal Qi before exhausting the limits of his current capabilities.

However, this performance did not take into account Yuan's Chaotic Essence, a different source of energy that, if utilized, could elevate the technique to an entirely new and far more devastating level.
Lord Zi looked at his damaged Immortal Qi with a profound expression on his face.

'What a devastating technique. He's only a Spirit Sovereign, but he's managed to damage my— a Golden Immortal's Immortal Qi to this extent. He might actually have the capability to slay a Bronze Immortal with this technique if he increased his cultivation a little more.' Lord Zi thought to himself.

"What do you think? How would you rank this technique?" Yuan suddenly asked, his back soaked in sweat. "What do you think? How would you rank this technique?" Yuan suddenly asked, his back soaked in sweat. Lord Zi pondered for a moment before finally responding, "This technique is undeniably at least Mythic-rank. In fact, it rivals the strongest Supreme-rank martial techniques I've encountered, and I would rank it as such. Moreover, I believe there is potential to refine and elevate this technique to Celestial-rank in the future."
"Supreme-rank, huh? I guess that means I qualify for a promotion, right?" Yuan said with a smile.

Lord Zi fell silent for a moment before laughing out loud, "You are correct. I will keep my word and promote you. Congratulations, you've become the highest-ranking member of our Martial Tower in a record-breaking time."
"Thank you."
"Now that you have full access to the Martial Tower, where would you like to go?" Lord Zi asked.
"What's on the highest floor?" Yuan asked.
"That would be my private living quarters. Unfortunately, it is only accessible to me," said Lord Zi.
"Ah, I see. Then I'll just take a look at the other floors."
"In that case, I will return to my own work. I can't wait to see how you'll contribute to the Martial Tower in the future."

After Lord Zi left, Yuan made his way to the 28th floor of the tower, where all the Mythic-rank techniques were stored. However, upon arriving at his destination, Yuan was surprised to see not a single Mythic-rank technique available.
He went to the 29th floor next, and sure enough, there was not a single Supreme-rank technique available. However, Yuan wasn't too shocked, only slightly disappointed.
"I bet the real Martial Tower would be filled with martial techniques on these floors," he muttered to himself.

Despite anticipating that the 30th floor would likely be empty, Yuan decided to investigate anyway. Upon arriving and spotting a single technique available on the otherwise vacant floor, he realized his effort had been well worth it.
Yuan immediately approached the technique, which rested elegantly on a stand crafted from fine jade. With curiosity and anticipation, he began reading the technique.
Sometime later.
<Shadow Veil learned>
[Shadow Veil]
[Rank: Celestial]
[Mastery Level: 1]
[Description: Envelope yourself in a veil of shadow, completely erasing your presence. While under the shadow's embrace, you become undetectable by divine sense and all detection techniques.]

Although Celestial Overlord Qiang had given him a technique that concealed his presence, Shadow Veil was incomparably better and could rival even Yingzi's natural invisible presence as a Shadow Dweller.
'Actually, this technique was most likely inspired by Shadow Dwellers and their lack of presence...' Yuan thought to himself.
'This technique is also perfect for this trial. With this technique, I will be able to spy on the Breakthrough Towers with more ease.'

The first thought that crossed Yuan's mind after acquiring the concealment technique was to use it to explore the highest floor of the Martial Tower—Lord Zi's living quarters. However, after giving it more consideration, Yuan decided to hold off until he had visited the other Breakthrough Towers. Sneaking into Lord Zi's quarters while he was still in the tower posed unnecessary risks.
'I should lure him out of the tower before I investigate his place,' Yuan concluded, formulating a more cautious plan.
With that in mind, Yuan decided to visit the next Breakthrough Tower.

Meanwhile, Tan Songyun was utterly bewildered after witnessing Yuan create a Supreme-rank technique in just a single month. Adding to her astonishment were the numerous other achievements he had demonstrated during the trial.

'Not only can he craft Empyrean-rank treasures with ease, but he's also capable of creating powerful martial techniques in such a short time. His talent is simply outrageous...' she thought, swallowing nervously as she recalled Yuan mentioning his previous lives.
